name: Battle_ActionModel_UpdateAttachmentVisibility
signature: int Battle_ActionModel_UpdateAttachmentVisibility(int * self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Per-frame visibility update for a battle action model: resolves the unit handle, matches it against the action slot and shows/hides the weapon attachment nodes through the model node API (nodes 0x16/0x18/0x1D/0x1E).
evidence: Named callees now pin the module: Battle_ActionModel_UpdateUnitVisibility, Battle_Model_FindAttachmentGridSlot, Battle_InsertActionSlot and Svc_ResolveObjectHandle; the address sits between Battle_ActionModel_DtorDelete, NotifyEffect and SetNodeStateB, and it is vtable 0x00782234 slot 7 like the other Battle_ActionModel members.

name: maybe_Field_UpdateEffectSlots
summary: Walks the 0x50x5 field effect/action slot table at +0xe8, and for each live slot (state 1..0x19, flags set) either dispatches the slot callback or retires it through Ui_CmdQueue_PushWidgetCommand. Called from the field actor-action sequence update with the scene slot table.
evidence: The only named caller is maybe_Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateMain (passes self[0x48b]), which fixes the module as field but not whether the slots are effects or actor actions; named callees are only Game_GetWork and the type-test helper, so the effect/action wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Battle_ResetActionSlots
signature: void maybe_Battle_ResetActionSlots(FieldSlots* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Zeroes the slot bookkeeping words at +0x2b0..+0x2d8, then compacts the live rows of the two parallel 0x50x5 slot arrays (f_e8/f_ec) and re-initialises freed rows with -1 sentinels and state 6.
evidence: The only named caller is maybe_Menu_SumPartyStats on &self->f_47a0, which contradicts the Battle_ prefix, while the row layout is identical to 0x00174E40 (field slot table). Module and purpose both stay unproven.

name: maybe_Actor_QueryInteraction
signature: unsigned int maybe_Actor_QueryInteraction(int* self, int id)
summary: Only runs while the battle-work flag at +0x4244 is set: resolves a data-manager record by id (f_44/f_34 gate), then resolves the generation-checked handle stored at self[0x44] and calls its first virtual. Returns the virtual's result.
evidence: Still no named caller (the earlier caller was a thunk of the same class), and the id space is the message/action row table func_0063E05C, so whether this is "interaction", an event target or a linked object cannot be decided; kept as-is.

name: Battle_Ui_FindTargetSlot
signature: void Battle_Ui_FindTargetSlot(BattleBalloonUi* self, const u8* filter, int* outSlot, int argument, int* outObj, int argument2)
summary: Scans the battle unit list at battlework+0x4260 for the first entry that matches the filter record (bytes +1/+2) and whose virtual queries pass, then returns the entry and its slot index through the out pointers.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Battle_Ui_Update calls it as FindTargetSlot(self,input,...,&out) inside the target-cursor update, and its plural sibling 0x003CC520 calls it to fill the multi-target list; the battle-work walk (+0x4260) is explicit in the body.

name: Battle_Ui_FindTargetSlots
summary: Builds the multi-target slot list for the current battle action: counts the usable actors, orders them with the battle RNG (func_001CA474 on +0x4218) and writes the chosen slot indices into out[8..].
evidence: Named caller maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update passes &self->f_14, and the body calls the now-named Battle_Ui_FindTargetSlot plus the battle RNG helper from FACTS; the surrounding addresses are the Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_* family.

name: Battle_Ui_SelectUnitAnimations
summary: Picks the battle unit's idle/pose animation: if the unit owns one of 0x10C/0x10D/0x10E/0xB3/0x78/0x7A it switches it through vtable+0x124, and for 0x10E applies the animation to every unit in the battle list.
evidence: Named caller Battle_Ui_UpdateLevelUpPopup calls it with just the UI object during the level-up popup, and the six animation ids plus the vtable+0x124 switch are all visible in the body.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_Step_DispatchFinishCommand
signature: int maybe_Battle_Ui_Step_DispatchFinishCommand(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Battle-UI sequence step: a countdown at +0x125C (reset to 0x102, -2 per call) gates a query of the child widget (vtable+0x18); when the child reports idle it sends slot command 0x79 through Model_SetSlotState, sets the done byte +0xd2 and returns 1.
evidence: The old Ui_Message_ prefix was wrong: the address sits in the Battle_Action_SpecialMove_*Start step table and the object uses the same +0x125C countdown / +0xd2 done-byte pattern as Battle_Ui_WaitForCondition79 (0x004BF430); +0x50 is a model slot, not a message window.

name: Battle_CheckActorCanAct
signature: u32 Battle_CheckActorCanAct(Actor* actor, u32 stateWord, u32 entityId, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns 0 when the unit must be skipped: state bits 8 or 10 are set, the actor record's +0xe4 is 5, or the actor's behaviour byte 0xB108 is 7/8; otherwise 1.
evidence: Named caller Ui_PartyPanel_AllMembersUnavailable calls it per party unit to decide whether any member can still act, which matches the predicate shape; the body is short and fully readable (no unaff_/coprocessor damage).

name: maybe_Ui_TextLayout_PickRandomRowByWidth
signature: int* maybe_Ui_TextLayout_PickRandomRowByWidth(UiTextLayout* self, u32 request, int* current)
summary: Collects the candidate rows whose measured text length exceeds the layout limit (0x63D178()->+0x147) and returns one of them at random; the request carries six text ids checked through the row object's vtable.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Ui_TextLayout_AppendCandidatesFiltered and the near-identical sibling maybe_Ui_TextLayout_PickRandomRowByTextWidth (0x0063930C) support the TextLayout module, but they do not explain the >limit comparison, so the verb stays a guess.

name: Field_GetActorAttachment
summary: Returns the actor's attachment sub-object: +0x8dc when the actor accepts type 0x11B and that pointer is set, otherwise +0x8e0, or 0 when neither exists.
evidence: Four named callers use it as an attachment getter (maybe_Actor_HandleSpecialEvent, maybe_FieldParty_UpdateTalkMemberState, maybe_FieldParty_UpdateActorAttachments, Model_SyncRotationToAttachment), and the body is the exact two-field fallback.

name: maybe_Actor_IsActiveState
summary: Predicate built from three virtual queries (vtable+0x10, +0x14, +0xD8) plus the type test: returns 0 only when the actor is not type 10 and not type 8.
evidence: No named caller; the neighbouring helpers (maybe_Actor_ShouldSkipUpdate, maybe_Actor_IsStateAnimAllowed) are all still unnamed, so neither the exact meaning of the three virtual bits nor the 'active' wording can be confirmed.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateAnimState
signature: unsigned int maybe_Actor_UpdateAnimState(int* self, unsigned int arg2, int whether)
summary: Advances the actor's animation-state machine for types 0x5C/0x5D/0x5E: compares the current frame (vtable+0x90) with the total (vtable+0x94), and past the half-way/2-frame threshold writes the direction field (+0x3c) and re-selects the animation through vtable+0x124.
evidence: The old 'ClassifyStateEx' implied a query, but the body mutates state: it stores through vtable+0x3c, calls vtable+0x124 to switch the animation and returns 2 after switching, which is animation-state stepping, not classification.

name: maybe_FieldParty_PlayStateSe
signature: void maybe_FieldParty_PlayStateSe(int * self, int model, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Plays a one-shot SE/voice for a model that entered state 0x76 or 0x11B, using the 32-entry bookkeeping table at +0xb1 (stride 0x1f: model, count, already-played byte) so each model plays once; the SE id comes from the record's +0x5a or defaults to 0xA0.
evidence: No attachment call exists in the body (the old 'PlaySeForAttachmentChange' was unsupported), and the neighbouring named functions are FieldParty_PlayCommonVoice / SelectMemberVoiceById, fixing the module as field-party sound, not the model attachment API.

name: maybe_FieldParty_UpdateSlotTypeFlags
summary: For each member (up to 8) and each of the 7 attachment slots, stores whether the member accepts the slot's type id into the per-member flag table at +0x1f2 and marks the slot used through vtable+0x120.
evidence: Named callers FieldParty_CtorB and FieldParty_ResetAllMembers both run it as part of party setup, and the body reads the slot type array at +0x1e4 and writes the 8x7 flag bytes exactly as the old summary said. The body still carries a lost base register (unaff_r6 points at the +0x1e4 type array), so confidence stays below 0.5 even though two named callers run it during party setup.

name: maybe_Menu_FindActorInListByType
summary: Walks an intrusive list and returns 1 as soon as an entry reports type 0x9c. Ghidra lost the list registers (unaff_r4/unaff_r5) and even the loop condition is misprinted, so the signature and module are placeholders.
evidence: No named caller or callee beyond the type-test helper; the decompilation still contains unaff_r4/unaff_r5 and the bogus arg1*0x2002 expression, so nothing new can be concluded.

name: Battle_CollectDisplayedUnits
signature: void Battle_CollectDisplayedUnits(int* list, int* head, unsigned int arg3)
summary: Walks the battle unit list at battlework+0x4260 and appends every live, handle-valid unit that is not busy (vtable+0xd8) and is neither type 8 nor 10 to the caller's display list via list vtable+0xb0 with kind 0xb.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitDisplay passes the battle unit list and 0xb, and the body pushes into the caller's list through vtable+0xb0; the handle/generation check uses the shared 0x007B80C0 table.

name: Ui_Row_SetIconSet
signature: void Ui_Row_SetIconSet(UiRow* self, int row, int* table, int useTable)
summary: Fills the seven icon bytes of a row (+0xe) either with 0 or with the icons resolved from the row's u16 id list, and marks each icon used through the icon table's vtable+0x120.
evidence: Its immediate neighbour Ui_Row_SetDefaultIconSet (0x0037EADC) is confidently named and does the same store with the default ids, so this is the parameterised twin; the 7-byte store and vtable+0x120 call are identical.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_SelectActor
summary: Member-widget slot: if the requested actor differs from the displayed one, or is in the dead/fled states (type 10/8), route the change through func_001F9B58; otherwise just re-select the actor.
evidence: The Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_Ctor at 0x003C3318 installs the same vtable and the neighbouring Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_PushActionMessage is already named; the body compares actor+0x10 and tests types 10/8.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_WaitForCondition79
summary: Battle-UI sequence step: while the countdown at +0x125C (default 0xCE) expires it checks the child widget (vtable+0x24) and whether the unit still reports type 0x79; when clear it sets the done byte +0xd2 and returns 1, otherwise it restarts the wait.
evidence: It shares the +0x125C countdown / +0xd2 done-byte step pattern with 0x004ECDF0, so the module is battle-UI, but there is still no named caller and 0x79 is an opaque type id, so the wording stays approximate.

name: Text_MessageWindow_ResolveLineStyle
signature: void Text_MessageWindow_ResolveLineStyle(TextWindow* self, TextLayout* layout, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Decides whether the pending message record can continue the current line: rejects plain/special style records, compares the layout's start/end cursor (vtable+0x90/+0x94) and asks the layout whether it accepts the row type before setting the line-resolved flag +0x19DE.
evidence: The old TalkWindow prefix did not match the class: the callers/callees are now named Text_MessageWindow_* (maybe_Text_TalkWindow_BuildLinesEx passes the shared layout, and Text_MessageWindow_UpdateLineEffects / ReleaseFragment sit in the same class), and the callees are maybe_Text_Style_IsPlainRecord / IsSpecialKind.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MessageWidget_SelectActor
summary: Message/member widget slot that switches the displayed actor: compares the actor pointer and checks types 10/8, then either re-selects the actor or routes the change through func_001F9B58. Same body as 0x003C332C.
evidence: The old 'PlayMemberSe_Pair' name was wrong - the function never plays a sound; its body is identical to Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_SelectActor (0x003C332C) and it lives in the Battle_Ui_PlayMemberSe/Text_Command balloon family, so only the owning widget class differs.

name: Ui_JockeyPanel_Close
summary: Closes the jockey panel: restores the input mode (system+0x30+0xE0), plays SE 0x3E and BGM/SE 0x7C, notifies the bound parts and triggers event command 0x1C.
evidence: The whole 0x002F5C..0x002F66 block is the named Ui_JockeyPanel_* family (Ui_JockeyPanel_ApplyVisualParams is already confident), and the close sequence (input restore + SE pair + event 0x1C) matches the old summary.

name: Ui_UpdateChildObject
summary: Ticks the window's optional child object at +0x324. When the child reports done it is destroyed, the command queue is advanced and either event command 9 is triggered or the window plays animation 0x65; otherwise the child's own update virtual runs.
evidence: The body is fully readable and the named neighbours are the other window tick steps (maybe_Ui_UpdateWindowOpen/State install the same vtable 0x00729A24, and Ui_CampMenu_Setup creates the window); no caller is named, so 0.5 rather than higher.

name: Field_ObjectSprite_ResolveName
summary: Builds the object sprite's display label: resolves the event and actor names, formats them as '%ls/%ls', publishes them as message args and stores the label in the object record; when the id is valid it triggers event command 0x13.
evidence: Named callers Field_ObjectSprite_CtorBase and maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_InitBaseClass run it while constructing the sprite, and the named callees Message_SetArg / Event_OnTriggerCommand plus the '%ls/%ls' literal confirm the label-building role.

name: maybe_Field_TalkBalloon_OpenSimpleMessage
signature: int maybe_Field_TalkBalloon_OpenSimpleMessage(TalkBalloon* self, int speaker, int style, int owner)
summary: Talk-balloon variant that lazily allocates the 0x1EB0-byte text buffer, plays the balloon SE and raises event command 0x14; it differs from 0x003D9484 only in the buffer globals and the command id.
evidence: The Field_TalkBalloon_* family around it is named (Ctor/Dtor/Delete/OpenMessage), so the module is right, but no caller shows which balloon style uses command 0x14, so the 'Simple' qualifier stays a guess.

name: Ui_UpdateWindowClose
signature: void Ui_UpdateWindowClose(UiWindow* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Per-frame close step of a layout window: updates the layout animation pair, and when the layout reports open without the 'closing' bit set plays the close command (0xC or 0xB depending on the object variant) and sets the child flags; otherwise advances the command queue.
evidence: The evidence of maybe_Ui_ObjectRef_IsFirstVariant now explicitly lists this function as one of the three window tick steps (Ui_UpdateWindowClose/Open/Confirm at 0x176A3C/0x176AD8/0x177000), and the body matches that close-step shape.

name: Ui_UpdateWindowConfirm
signature: void Ui_UpdateWindowConfirm(UiWindow* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Confirm/cancel variant of the window tick: when the layout reports mode 1 and the stored event-command id at +0x320 is not -1 it triggers that command and sets the child flags; otherwise it advances the command queue.
evidence: Same named trio as 0x00176A3C (Ui_UpdateWindowClose/Open/Confirm) plus named callees Ui_Widget_Update, Ui_CommandQueue_Advance and Event_OnTriggerCommand; the difference from the close step is exactly the stored +0x320 command.

name: maybe_Battle_ApplyUnitPartMask
signature: void maybe_Battle_ApplyUnitPartMask(BattleUnit* self, u32 maskIn, u32 arg3, u32 flags)
summary: Applies a part/attachment selection to a battle unit: merges the caller mask with the model flag word, probes the primary/secondary attachment tables and forwards the successful transform to the render model, otherwise falls back to the default part update.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitPartMask passes (self, mask, index, flags), and the touch points are now named (maybe_Battle_ApplyPartMaskToModel, maybe_Battle_ReleaseUnitHandle, Event_OnTriggerCommand); the body's table probes match the old summary. Ghidra lost the caller mask register (unaff_r6 in the mask merge), so the name stays maybe_ until the disassembly is read.

name: Ui_JockeyPanel_OnConfirm
summary: Confirm handler of the jockey panel: if the selection is not accepted yet it triggers event command 0x1B and switches the panel to state 3; otherwise it plays the cached sound and switches to state 3.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_SetState5 is the next row of the same step table, and the Ui_JockeyPanel_* family plus Ui_GetCore/Event_OnTriggerCommand callees are all named now.

name: maybe_Ui_PlayWindowSe
signature: void maybe_Ui_PlayWindowSe(UiWindow* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Minimal window tick: updates the layout animation and, when the layout is open, triggers the event command stored at self+0x320 and sets the child flags (done at +0x10, step 0xD).
evidence: No caller and the command goes through the generic Event_OnTriggerCommand, so whether +0x320 is an SE id (as the name says) or a generic event command cannot be decided; the step shape is the same as the named close/confirm variants.

name: Ui_IconRequest_Update
summary: State machine of an icon request: while not done/busy it dispatches on the record's kind byte (1..7) to start the matching icon path (case 2 applies the face icon through 0x003103A8, cases 3/7 raise event commands) and then marks the request busy.
evidence: The named callee maybe_Ui_ApplyFaceIconToWork is the case-2 face-icon path and the named Event_OnTriggerCommand covers the 2/4/5/8 command ids, so the icon-request reading is supported even though the function is only reached through a vtable.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_OnBreakCommand
summary: Actor-side break command: when the UI overlay mode byte is not 7 it triggers event command 0x18, otherwise it plays the actor's default animation.
evidence: The neighbourhood (Field_Actor_PlayBreakEffectAll at 0x00364264, maybe_Field_Object_PlayDefaultAnim at 0x00364014) explains the 'Break' wording, but no caller shows who issues the command, so the name stays a guess.

name: Field_Gadget_UpdateDrag
summary: Updates a gadget the player is dragging: while state 1 it adds the touch delta to the gadget position, clamps it, and when the touch is released switches to state 2 and triggers event command 0x15.
evidence: The Field_Gadget_* family around it is named (Field_Gadget_Ctor, GetTouchPoint, IsTouchOutside) and the body reads the touch object at work+0x54->+0x20 (+0x1c5), exactly the drag state machine the old summary described.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_ApplyShapeToTarget
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Overlay_ApplyShapeToTarget(FieldObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 geometry, u32 mask)
summary: Resolves the target under the cursor through the overlay entry list (maybe_Ui_Overlay_FindTargetUnderCursor), then applies the viewport/shape attribute of the matching entry kind to the model part.
evidence: The old Field_ prefix was unsupported: the caller is maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitPartMask, the callees are the Ui_Overlay_* family (FindTargetUnderCursor, CheckEntryPlacement, ModelPart_ApplyAttribute) and the function reads the touch flag f_1c5.

name: Ui_ItemInfoWindow_Create
summary: Creates (once per UI core) the shared item-info window: installs the item-info vtable, registers its node list and sub-objects and returns the window base pointer.
evidence: The old Field_FindJockeyObject name was wrong: the body is a constructor that installs class pointer 0x00761E68, which is the word before the item-info window vtable row 0x00761E78 used by the confidently named Ui_ItemInfoWindow_Update (0x002F6950, same class block as Ui_ItemInfoWindow_OnEvent and the two dtors at 0x002F6B48/0x002F6B74). Every named caller is a window that displays item details (Ui_ShopWindow_Ctor, Ui_PrizeWindow_Init, Ui_EquipTextWindow_Ctor, Ui_PokerWindow_Payout, maybe_Ui_MainMenuText_SetWindowState).

name: Ui_SkillPanel_UpdateFrame
signature: void Ui_SkillPanel_UpdateFrame(UiSkillPanel* self, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int arg3)
summary: Advances the skill panel's open animation frame counter (0..0x36) and, once it passes the halfway frame 0x12, rebinds the 'renkei' pane animation and starts the follow-up animation; sends SE 0x34 on the way.
evidence: It installs vtable 0x0072A050, shared with the already-named Ui_SkillPanel_ApplyState / InitRowList / OpenClose, and the f_2460 frame counter plus the 0x12 rebind are visible in the body (tail has Ghidra bad-instruction artefacts).

name: maybe_Ui_WorldMapMarker_Init
signature: int maybe_Ui_WorldMapMarker_Init(u32* out, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises one world-map marker/cursor record: stores the id, registers the 0x10-byte sub-object and fills the position/scale fields with the -4096 sentinel, the flag bytes at +0x88 and the default table copied into +0x94.
evidence: The neighbours are now named world-map code (Ui_WorldMap_ReleaseResources, DestructorBody, DestroyThunk), which fixes the module, but no caller distinguishes a marker from another world-map record and the function has no named callee besides Ui_NodeList_Register.

name: Ui_IconFlashing_Ctor
signature: void Ui_IconFlashing_Ctor(void* self, unsigned int owner)
summary: Constructor of the flashing-icon object: runs the shared 0x1EF-byte base constructor, installs the icon vtable and stores the owner pointer at +0x1C.
evidence: Its immediate neighbour Ui_IconFlashing_SetEnabled (0x00381C14) is confidently named and operates on the same object, and named callers maybe_Ui_FieldScreen_Init and Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyText both create it as the flashing message icon.

name: maybe_Container_HandleList_Ctor
signature: ContainerHandleList* maybe_Container_HandleList_Ctor(ContainerHandleList* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Builds an object owning a small intrusive list plus resource handles: writes the recovered handle-list descriptor, registers the element list (element size 0x14), zeroes the handle array and stores a ref-counted resource at +0x18.
evidence: The mirror dtor 0x00445710 and named caller maybe_Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel support the shape, but Ghidra reports bad instruction data at the tail and the descriptor name is itself recovered, so the exact class stays uncertain.

name: Ui_TimeWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the clock/time window: installs vtable 0x007800C0, sets up the two intrusive list heads and chains the pane, text and node-list sub-object constructors, returning the window base.
evidence: The old StatusWindow name was wrong: vtable 0x007800C0 is the one installed by Ui_TimeWindow_Dtor (0x0061BC4C), and the whole neighbourhood is named Ui_TimeWindow_* (BindPanes, IsClockReady, RenderClock).

name: Ui_List_Create
summary: Creates a UI list object: allocates the base, installs the list vtable, initialises the two intrusive list heads and the 0x10-element child table, and returns the outer object.
evidence: Named callers maybe_Ui_SenrekiWindow_CtorB (stores it at +0x2a0) and maybe_Ui_IndexPairTable_Ctor use it as a list constructor, and the body's list-head self references match the named Ui_List_* helpers nearby.

name: maybe_Ui_SimpleWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor for a small window object: runs the base constructor, installs vtable 0x007597A4, sets the default two-word values at +0x11c..+0x124 and chains the child part constructors.
evidence: Only the named caller maybe_Ui_Screen_CreateChildWindows shows it is a child window; 'Simple' is a guess about which window class this is, and its only named callees are the generic Ui_NodeList_Register chain.

name: Ui_ListWindow_Create
summary: Creates the list window: installs vtable 0x0076216C, initialises the intrusive list heads and the priority-ordered object, and returns the window base.
evidence: The old Field_CreateWorldList name was wrong: vtable 0x0076216C is the list-window table whose destructor is maybe_Ui_ListWindow_Dtor at 0x002F77A0 (same class, 0x68 bytes later).

name: Field_CreateEffectSprite
signature: void Field_CreateEffectSprite(FieldObject* self, int* arg2, int* arg3)
summary: Attaches a sprite child to a field object: merges the caller's point/rect records into a sprite descriptor, takes the world's 2D mode into account and adds the child through Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild, storing the handle at +0x29c.
evidence: Six named callers use it from the sprite-actor parameter constructors (Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromParams and its B/C/Ex variants, Field_SpawnObjectVariant) and the named callee Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild is the actual attach.

name: maybe_Script_ThumbStub_2CC714
signature: void maybe_Script_ThumbStub_2CC714(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, int* loop, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, int* refcounted)
summary: Unrecovered Thumb function in the script/fs block: it walks a 0x14-byte record array, writes one byte and copies two 8-byte halves per record, and releases up to six ref-counted temporaries on exit. Name is a placeholder only.
evidence: The old Ui_ prefix was wrong: every named callee is Squirrel/FS code (Script_ReadSerializedValue, Script_ObjectPtr_Assign, Script_ReadClosureRef, Fs_UnmountByName), but Ghidra hits bad instruction data and lost all argument registers, so the operation stays unknown.

name: Script_ObjectVector_Trim
summary: Trims a Squirrel object vector back to `keep` entries: pops records from the tail, moves the still-live ones (non-null tag) into the secondary vector and releases the dropped references.
evidence: Three named callers now pin it to the Squirrel compiler (Script_SqCompiler_Compile, Script_SqCompiler_FunctionExp, Script_SqCompiler_Statement), which pass the compiler's value stack and a keep index.

name: maybe_Script_VM_RunClosure
signature: void maybe_Script_VM_RunClosure(unsigned int vm, unsigned int closure, void* fn, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Large Squirrel VM helper (0x1480 bytes) that prepares a call frame, invokes a closure through the serialized-value helpers and releases the temporary references. Only the entry block is recovered.
evidence: Named callees Script_ReadSerializedValue / Script_ReadClosureRef / Script_ObjectPtr_Assign confirm Squirrel VM code, but Ghidra recovered only the entry block of a 5 KB function, so 'RunClosure' remains a guess.

name: maybe_Script_SqValueList_GetItem
signature: int maybe_Script_SqValueList_GetItem(SqValueList* self, u32 arg2, int index, SQObjectPtr* out)
summary: Element accessor for the Squirrel value list: tests whether slot `index` of the value array is the tagged null (0x01000001) and, if not, copies it into the caller's SQObjectPtr; returns whether a value was copied.
evidence: The body is fully readable and consistent with a GetItem slot, but the readable signature has an unused arg2 and no named caller, so neither the exact vtable role nor the parameter order can be confirmed.

name: Field_FindActorEntryByModel
summary: Returns the actor's appearance entry: looks up the actor record by id, reads its model-variant flags byte and scans the 0x38-byte entry table at record+0x3c for the entry whose +0x30 matches, falling back to the record itself.
evidence: Named callers Text3D_UpdateBillboardTransform, Text_BuildRowForActor, maybe_Field_ActorEntry_Copy and the battle transform code all use the result as the per-model appearance entry, matching the body's flag comparison.

name: maybe_Actor_GetEquipAppearanceType
summary: Returns the appearance/variant type used to pick an actor's model parts: reads the member's two equipped items (slots 0 and 1), maps the first item's category byte (+0x29) to 1..15 and bumps it by one when both items share the category; returns 0xFF when no item is equipped or 0 for a few special actor ids.
evidence: The old Ui_GetItemIconType name was wrong: named callers pass the result straight into the appearance table (maybe_Field_FindActorEntryByModel compares it with entry+0x30, maybe_Field_CreateActorRenderObject uses it as a flags byte), and the body resolves equipped item ids through func_006292F0, not UI icons.

name: Ui_Hud_HideSequence
summary: Step-driven HUD hide used when a full-screen message/menu opens: hides the cursor, waits for the layout animation, sets the render flag, unloads the common pack and finally clears the ten HUD element flags at +0x114..+0x11D.
evidence: Named callees Gfx_GetContext, Pack_GetManager, Ui_LoadingScreen_IsFinished and Ui_GetCore now cover every step of the state machine, and its mirror maybe_Ui_Hud_ShowSequence is documented as the inverse.

name: maybe_Ui_CloseScreenOnButton
summary: Screen tick that closes the screen when the player presses the mapped button: tests the button query, consumes it and requests animation 9 (the back/cancel clip) on the screen's animator; always returns 1.
evidence: No named caller, and the callee that consumes the press is now named Ui_SceneFlow_BindSlotResources, which does not match a button query - so both the 'button' and the 'close' reading rest on the old evidence only.

name: Field_Action_MoveCollide
summary: Moves the actor with collision: builds a rotation from the camera-relative input direction, adds velocity to the actor node and pushes it out of the hit normal when it runs into geometry.
evidence: Named callees Field_GetCombinedMoveVector and Math_QuatFromAxisAngle are exactly the vector/quaternion helpers this body uses, and the field-action class family (Field_Action_Walk/Move) around it is named.

name: Field_Actor_UpdateBehaviour
summary: Chooses and ticks the actor's next behaviour (idle, walk, run or turn) from the distance to its goal, the map-section range and the actor flags, and stops the task when the chosen behaviour reports failure.
evidence: Five named callers now treat it as the behaviour tick (Field_Actor_UpdateInputDirection tail-calls it, Field_Action_PlayStepSound, Monster_FieldBehaviour_SkullDash, maybe_Field_DragonJumpAction_UpdateCamera, Actor_SelectAttractAnimation), and the vtable dispatch +0x2c/+0x30/+0x34/+0x38 is visible in the body.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateIdleAnimationPair
summary: Runs the idle/attract animation step on the two objects registered in the actor manager (work+0x54 -> +0x1c and +0x20) and ORs their results, so a non-zero return means one of them is still animating.
evidence: The old Ui_Menu_IsBusy name was wrong on both halves: the body reads work+0x54 (the actor manager, per the established work layout, not the UI manager at +0x48) and calls the actor animation helpers on its two children, ignoring its own argument.

name: maybe_Monster_FieldBehaviour_UpdateAttack
summary: Attack step of a field monster: tracks the player's visibility, runs the physics step and, when the monster has come to rest after the dash, falls back to the attract/idle animation.
evidence: Named neighbours (Monster_FieldBehaviour_SkullDash, maybe_Monster_FieldBehaviour_UpdateChase / PlayRunEffect / TrackActionSlot) fix the module, but there is still no caller and no nameable callee that proves this slot is the attack behaviour.

name: Field_ActorMove_Integrate
summary: Integrates the stored direction and speed into the actor position each frame (with the slower factor when f_51 is set), turns the actor towards the direction and finishes the move through the actor action helper once the motion reports arrival.
evidence: Named caller Actor_SelectAttractAnimation and the whole maybe_Field_ActorMove_* family (CreateTask, Cancel, InitDirection, ClampDirection, BeginStep) around it confirm the move-task class; the body is clean.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_UpdateApproach
summary: Approach action: picks an animation by actor type/state, moves the actor forward with deceleration and switches to the attract animation when the timer expires.
evidence: No caller; only Actor_SelectAttractAnimation is named among the callees, and the neighbouring functions are unnamed field-action classes, so 'approach' is still an inference from the motion maths.

name: maybe_Field_Action_FinishCutIfDone
summary: Cut action step: when the owner actor reports the motion finished, switches it back to its attract/idle animation (shared template body, same as 0x001BA46C / 0x00302184 and five others).
evidence: 'CanFinishCut' was wrong because the function returns nothing and actively finishes the action; the Cut association comes from the named neighbours in the same block (maybe_Field_Action_StartCut/EndCut/CreateCut), while the body itself is the shared finish template.

name: maybe_Field_Action_FinishDigIfDone
summary: Dig action step: same shared finish template as the Cut variant - when the owner actor reports the motion finished it switches back to the attract/idle animation (identical body to 0x001BA350).
evidence: Same reasoning as 0x001BA350: 'CanFinish...' misdescribed a void action; the Dig association comes from the neighbouring maybe_Field_Action_StartDig/EndDig/CreateDig/CreateNut block, not from the body.

name: maybe_Actor_FinishMotionIfDone
summary: Generic action step: when the referenced actor reports its motion finished, switch it back to the attract/idle animation. Identical body to 0x001BA350/0x00302184 (shared template copy).
evidence: The old 'ResetBattlePose' invented a battle meaning that nothing supports - the neighbourhood is UI cursor/list code and the body is the plain finish template, so the honest name only states the observed behaviour.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_FinishLanding
summary: Landing/finish step: when the actor reports its motion finished it switches to the attract animation with selection 1, then always returns 1 (step complete). Shared template body with a different argument.
evidence: The 'landing' wording comes from the named neighbours (Actor_Action_Move_InterpolateToTarget, maybe_Actor_Action_Move_UpdateAnimation, Actor_UpdateBankingTilt); the body alone is the common finish template, so the class slot stays unproven.

name: Field_Action_PitfallFall
summary: Falling step of the pitfall trap: while the lid animation is closed it accelerates the object downward, and once the open animation (0xD) plays it disables collision and lets the object drop.
evidence: Named caller maybe_Field_Action_Pitfall_DtorDelete plus the neighbouring maybe_Field_Action_PitfallSetState and the body's 0xD/0xE animation checks and collision-disable virtual settle the pitfall-fall role.

name: maybe_Field_Action_FinishIfDoneEx
summary: Door-action step: when the actor reports the motion finished it switches back to the attract/idle animation. Byte-identical to 0x00300A44, hence the Ex suffix.
evidence: The named caller Field_Action_OpenDoor_DeletingDtor confirms it belongs to the door action, but the body is a template copy and the Ex suffix only distinguishes it from the identical 0x00300A44.

name: maybe_ActorAction_UpdateAttract
summary: Actor-action vtable step (slot 3 of 0x007687EC): if the actor reports its motion finished, switch to the attract/idle animation. Same template body as the other finish steps.
evidence: No named caller; the vtable slot and the surrounding maybe_ActorAction_* / Monster_FieldBehaviour_* classes are the only evidence, and the body is the shared template.

name: maybe_Ui_SpriteMarker_FinishAttract
summary: UI sprite-marker step: when the marker actor's motion finished, switch it back to the attract animation (selection 0). Same template body as the other finish steps.
evidence: The class comes from the named neighbour Ui_SpriteMarker_SetTargetFromActor; the body cannot prove the 'attract' wording, so the guess stays below certainty.

name: maybe_Field_ActorBehavior_SetAttractAnimation
summary: Actor-behaviour vtable step (0x00776B90): if the actor reports its motion finished, switch to the attract animation with selection 1.

name: maybe_Ui_Message_PlayAttractAnim
summary: Message-window vtable step: if the actor referenced at +0x28 reports its motion finished, switch it to the attract animation with selection 1; its named neighbour maybe_Ui_Message_PlayIdleAnim is the mirror.
evidence: Only the neighbouring maybe_Ui_Message_PlayIdleAnim distinguishes the two variants, and both are still unnamed, so the attract/idle split is an inference from the argument 1 vs 0.

The new handle value is still an unaff_r9 artefact, so the binding is visible but the stored value is not fully recovered.

name: Ui_PokerWindow_ConfirmBet
summary: Confirm step of the bet: copies the caller's handler pair, clears the dialog state, pops the bet window and binds the card text for the selected value.
evidence: Poker vtable 0x007294D0 and the named callees Ui_CasinoWin_PopWindowStack / maybe_Ui_PokerWindow_BindCardText; the body only differs from HandleBet in the pop kind (3).

name: Ui_PokerWindow_BindCardText
signature: void Ui_PokerWindow_BindCardText(PokerWindow* self, int visible, int value)
summary: Binds the currently drawn card to the window: toggles the card pane visibility, sets its value and, when the id is an equipment item, writes the card's name text.
evidence: Seven named callers (Ui_PokerWindow_Payout, Ui_PokerWindow_MoveCursor, Ui_PrizeWindow_Init, confirm/close/bet handlers) all call it as (self, visible, value), and the body sets the card pane's +0x135/+0x94 and the item-name text.

name: maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_CtorWidgets
signature: void* maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_CtorWidgets(void* self, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int b, int c)
summary: Third-stage constructor of the jackpot screen (Thumb): creates the widget/toggle objects and sets the display values at f_DD8..f_DE4. The decompilation is damaged.
evidence: The body still contains unaff_r4/unaff_r5/unaff_r7 and in_s1/in_s16 register artefacts and the 'CtorWidgets' wording is a placeholder, so nothing new can be concluded about which widgets are built.

name: Ui_MapWindow_Init
summary: Initialises the world-map window: loads ui_map_param.bxon as a smart handle, finds the 'stamp_L' pane in the layout and builds the stamp sub-object at +0x124.
evidence: The 'ui_map_param.bxon' and 'stamp_L' string literals are in the body, and the named callees Ui_AnimRef_Bind / Ui_QuestWindow_InitPanes belong to the map/quest window family.

name: Ui_BeginLoadTask
signature: void Ui_BeginLoadTask(void* self, u8 mode, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Starts loading one UI element: stores the mode byte at +8, releases the previous request handle, allocates a 0x21C-byte page and opens chunk type 0xE for it, then marks the element's state byte as 6 (loading).
evidence: The named caller maybe_Ui_DataPanel_BeginOpenWithRecord starts a load with it and the named inverse 0x00248CCC clears the same handle and sets the state back to 0; the callee is the now-named Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple.

name: Ui_ResourceSet_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a UI resource bundle: installs the vtable, releases the four reference-counted handles at +0xC..+0x18 and the one at +0x1C, and destroys the 4-word handle array.
evidence: Named callers maybe_Ui_SimpleWindow_Dtor and maybe_Ui_HandleSet_Dtor both run it on an embedded bundle, and the callees are the now-named handle-release helpers.

name: Battle_Popup_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the animated battle number widget: clears the state, releases the resource handle, wipes the three 0x50-byte animation slots, disposes the list and frees the block.
evidence: The named ctor Battle_Popup_Ctor at 0x00469FF4 creates exactly this object, and the callees are the now-named handle/list release helpers; no caller because it is only reached through the vtable.

name: maybe_Ui_HandleSet_ClearAll
summary: Releases and invalidates all twelve handles of the set (nine at +4, three at +0x28) by writing the free generation tag, then destroys the two 4-word arrays.
evidence: 'Retag' misdescribed it: every slot is released through Pack_FreeHandleEntry and then marked invalid (generation 0xFFFFF), which is clearing, not retagging; the named caller maybe_Ui_Sequence_Dtor runs it as teardown.

name: Ui_JockeyPanel_Clear
signature: void Ui_JockeyPanel_Clear(UIWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Resets the jockey panel: destroys the embedded preview holder, releases the preview handle at +0x138, binds the new character by id and clears the cursor/scroll fields.
evidence: The named caller maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithGauge and the named callee maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_BindCharacter match the reset sequence, and the Ui_JockeyPanel_* family is named.

name: Ui_Resource_Delete
summary: Deleting destructor of the small UI resource holder: installs the vtable, releases the handle at +4, clears the state bytes and frees the block.
evidence: Named callees Pack_FreeHandleEntry / Pack_ReleaseHandle and the sibling maybe_Ui_Resource_ReleaseAndReset (0x003B3C74) confirm the resource-holder teardown; the body matches the old summary.

name: Ui_StreetPassText_LoadTables
summary: Loads and caches the two StreetPass text tables (stpass_text.bxon and spirit_skill_text.bxon) used by the profile card, validating the record type and minimum record count and keeping one record handle per table.
evidence: Both literal file names are present in the body and the named callees (Fs/Pack handle helpers) are the load path, so the StreetPass reading is directly evidenced.

name: Res_HandleClear
summary: Clears a two-word resource handle: drops the reference held in the second word through the engine refcount table, zeroes the first word and marks the slot free while keeping its generation tag.
evidence: The named caller maybe_Ui_ReleaseLayoutResources uses it during teardown, and the body is the standard validate/release/invalidate block used by every handle owner in this module.

name: Battle_UnitModel_AssignHandleA
summary: Reference-counted handle assignment for the battle unit model field at +0x13C: releases the old generation, adds a reference to the new handle and stores it.
evidence: The old Monster_ prefix was wrong: the whole block is the named Battle_UnitModel_* class (MoveBy, Update, UpdateParts, SetAlpha, SetPosition), so this is a Battle_UnitModel setter; the A suffix distinguishes the +0x13C twin from the +0x138 one.

name: Battle_UnitModel_AssignHandleB
summary: Same reference-counted handle assignment as 0x0042A3B4 but for the battle unit model field at +0x138.
evidence: Identical body to 0x0042A3B4 with self->f_138, and both live inside the named Battle_UnitModel_* block, so the Monster_ prefix was wrong.

name: Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchorScreen
signature: void Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchorScreen(BattleBalloonUi* self, char* anchor, int flag, u32 argument)
summary: Converts a member/slot anchor record into a screen-space position for battle balloons, handling the three anchor modes of this module through the widget virtuals.
evidence: Six named callers (Battle_Ui_Balloon_UpdateState, Battle_Ui_Balloon_MoveToAnchor, Battle_Sequence_Update, FieldParty_ComputeFormationBounds, maybe_Battle_Ui_RowPanel_UpdateB/MemberB) all use it to place balloons or row panels.

name: maybe_FieldParty_RegisterMemberModel
summary: Registers the character id of the actor occupying a party slot with the battle scene model manager, but only while the battle-work mode byte at +0x4244 is 1.
evidence: Named callers pass (slot, actor->f_768 & 0xffff) consistently, but the callee is now named maybe_BattleScene_ResolveModelSize, which sounds like a query rather than a registration, so the verb stays uncertain.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateMemberPoses
summary: Applies the pose/attachment update to the leader when the sub-mode flag +0x2a6 is set, otherwise to every non-enemy member of the sequence.
evidence: Five named callers (Battle_ActionSequence_Update, Battle_Ui_Balloon_MoveToAnchor, maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_UpdateB, FieldParty_ComputeFormationBounds, Battle_Ui_UpdateBalloonMotion) run it from the sequence update path.

name: Menu_InitFromParams
signature: void Menu_InitFromParams(MenuState* self, int mode, Param* parameter, unsigned char* flags)
summary: Initialises the menu/battle command state from an event/talk parameter block: stores the mode flags, selects the window object, resolves the actor record and resets the entry lists and counters.
evidence: Named callers Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene0, BattleScene_RebuildScene and Menu_SetEntryDisplayMode all set the state up from a parameter block, and the body reads the parameter bytes into the f_4244.. block.

name: Menu_CloseWindow
summary: Closes a menu window: clears its display state, sends the close notification with the window parameters, stops the associated message UI and releases the window object.
evidence: The named callees Menu_SetEntryDisplayMode, Ui_GetCore, Gfx_Scene2D_ResetScroll and maybe_Party_InitBattleSlots are exactly the close sequence in the body, and two named callers use it while tearing the menu down.

name: maybe_Menu_RebuildEffectList
summary: Rebuilds the per-actor effect/animation descriptors for the currently inactive actors: counts them, allocates a table and fills one 0x10-byte record per actor, then frees it.
evidence: The named callers are battle UI refresh paths (Battle_UiFlow_RebuildEffectList, maybe_Battle_RefreshBattleUi) which suggests a battle module, while the named callee Menu_BuildEffectCommandList suggests the menu - so the prefix is unresolved and the 2.3 KB body is only partly readable.

name: Gfx_Scene_Shutdown
summary: Shuts the scene down: hides every child drawable, releases either the composite/sub-object set or the battle scene models depending on the mode byte, releases the six helper objects and resets the per-scene state.
evidence: Named callees now cover the teardown (Ui_CompositeWindow_ReleaseHandles, Ui_ReleaseSubObjects, BattleScene_ReleaseSceneModels, Container_List_DestroyAll, Gfx_Scene2D_ResetScroll) and four named field-actor reset functions call it.

name: Actor2D_ResetPartsIfIdle
signature: void Actor2D_ResetPartsIfIdle(Actor2D* actor, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 thread)
summary: If the part id stored at +0x2C8 still resolves to a live object, stops its animation and update and clears the part bookkeeping fields +0x2B4 and +0x308.
evidence: Six named Actor2D_* callers (CreateFromParamA/B/C/D, OnStateNotify, maybe_Actor_OnEvent) all run it at the end of the 2D actor setup paths, and the body is a single resource check plus two virtuals.

name: Model_Attach_SetFadeRange
signature: void Model_Attach_SetFadeRange(ModelAttachSlot* slot, s32 start, s32 end)
summary: Sets the attachment's fade/alpha range: stores the start/end in +0x5BC/+0x5C0/+0x5C4 (keeping the previous value in +0x5B4/+0x5B8), falls back to the -1.0 constant when the end is negative, then recurses into every child of the +0x6B0 list.
evidence: The named neighbours Model_AttachSlot_Show/HideIfVisible/Dtor and Model_Attach_UpdateAnimationFrame operate on the same slot layout, and named callers (Model_Equip_UpdateNodeVisibility, maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateWeaponAttachRange) use it on attach slots; note the float arguments are still lost (in_s0/in_s1).

name: Ui_Label_SetFromShortTriple
signature: void Ui_Label_SetFromShortTriple(FieldObject* self, const u16* values, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Writes up to three text lines from a u16 triple into the label's text slots (+0x700..+0x708), skipping 0xFFFF entries, then resolves the label's character/font and updates the mesh/anim assignment.
evidence: Four named callers (Battle_ActionSequence_Update, Battle_Sequence_Update, maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_UpdateB, maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyLabels) pass a label plus the record's u16 triple at +0x1fe.
